findings.title: Preserve the original light-theme text shade
findings.body: This text was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement makes the light-theme branch 70% lighter. `dark-light-choose` uses its first argument for light themes, so this changes the link to a much lighter, potentially low-contrast color instead of preserving its existing appearance. Use 30% for the first argument and 70% for the secondary-based dark-theme argument.

findings.title: Keep the group member name's original lightness
findings.body: The original color used `$primary` at 30% lightness, but the replacement uses 50% for the light-theme branch. Since `dark-light-choose` selects its first argument for light themes, group member names become lighter than before. Preserve 30% in the first argument and use the complementary 70% secondary-based shade for dark themes.

findings.title: Keep the group member name's original lightness
findings.body: The original color used `$primary` at 30% lightness, but the replacement uses 50% for the light-theme branch. Since `dark-light-choose` selects its first argument for light themes, group member names become lighter than before on mobile. Preserve 30% in the first argument and use the complementary 70% secondary-based shade for dark themes.

findings.title: Preserve the topic-map heading shade
findings.body: This heading previously used `$primary` at 20% lightness, but its light-theme branch now uses 50%. `dark-light-choose` selects that first branch for light themes, so the heading becomes substantially lighter than its previous color. Keep 20% for the first argument and use 80% of `$secondary` for the dark-theme branch.

findings.title: Preserve the custom-message length text shade
findings.body: The original text color used `$primary` at 70% lightness, while the replacement uses 30% for the light-theme branch. `dark-light-choose` selects its first argument for light themes, making this text much darker than before. Keep 70% for the first argument and use 30% of `$secondary` for the dark-theme branch.
